ev.q: Among adult e-cigarette users overall, 29.4% also were current cigarette smokers, 40.3% were former cigarette smokers, and 30.3% had never been cigarette smokers.
Among e-cigarette users aged 18–24 years, 16.3% were current smokers, 22.3% were former smokers, and 61.4% had never been cigarette smokers.
In 2021, 4.5% of U.S. adults were current e-cigarette users.
Younger e-cigarette users were more likely to have never smoked cigarettes, and older e-cigarette users were more likely to be current or former cigarette smokers.

ev.q: Among those aged ≥45 years, 42.7% were current smokers, 50.1% were former smokers, and 7.2% had never smoked cigarettes.
The percentage of adults aged ≥18 years currently using e-cigarettes was 4.5%.
Younger e-cigarette users were more likely to have never smoked cigarettes, and older e-cigarette users were more likely to be current or former cigarette smokers.

notes: QuickStats; NHIS estimates presumably survey-weighted but weighting is not stated, so no weighting procedure is recorded. Age contrasts rest on side-by-side percentages with CI error bars; no test is described.
